meta.title: JOURNEYWAYS | The Board Game
meta.description: JOURNEYWAYS is a UBC-rooted research project exploring identity and agency through collaborative storytelling. Learn how to play the board game: rules, setup, solo and group play for secular, gender-neutral self-inquiry.

meta.og_description: How to play JOURNEYWAYS: setup, turns, and how a session ends. Five card categories, a buildable map, no winning, no losing.

hero.cover_alt: JOURNEYWAYS rulebook cover: a round watercolour labyrinth above the Journeyways wordmark and the tagline a board game about becoming.
hero.title: How to play.
hero.tagline: Setup, turns, and how a session ends.
hero.intro: JOURNEYWAYS is not about winning or losing. The rules below are a frame to start from. Bend them, break them, write your own. The single fixed rule is that everyone at the table agrees.

decks.intro: Cards are shuffled together, but then spread into three or more piles. Players choose which pile to pick from. They know the kind of card they will get, but not exactly which one.

need: For 1 to 6 players, plus a facilitator. If more people want to play, use a second game set.
Board tiles (47), plus a blank tile (1).
steps: Shuffle all cards together and place them face down in three piles.
Pick one card and place it apart face up. This will be the Discard pile.
Shuffle all the board tiles and place them face down in three piles.
Each player takes one player token.
Choose together who starts and a rough turn order. Turns don't need to be rigid: anyone can play when they feel like it, or sit a turn out.
The starting player picks a tile from any pile and places it in the middle of the table. This is the first tile, where the journey begins.
Taking turns, each player picks a tile from any pile and places it adjacent to another previously placed tile. If it's a blank tile, put it back in the pile and pick again.
All players place their tokens on the first tile.
setup.figure_alt: Top-down photo of a JOURNEYWAYS setup ready to begin: a four-by-four grid of map tiles in the foreground, the character booklet and a meeple case to the left, and a pile of character cards behind them on a wooden surface.

turn.intro_html: Each turn has three phases: Explore, Pick, and Reflect. Turns follow the rough order you agreed on, but stay loose: play when you feel ready, or sit a turn out.

phases.title: Explore
phases.body_html: Two options. Pick a map tile and place it adjacent to another one. If you pick a blank tile, you have to create it before placing it. Or use a sticky note to draw a new map tile (whatever you want) and place it on top of an existing one where no player is located. After placing your tile, you can move one or two spaces in any direction.

phases.title: Pick
phases.body_html: Pick a card from any pile, even the Discard pile. {{deck:movement.colour}} cards are movement, {{deck:countdown.colour}} cards are pass of time, {{deck:reflection.colour}} cards are quotes, {{deck:encounter.colour}} cards are encounters, {{deck:group.colour}} cards are group events.

phases.title: Reflect
phases.body_html: If you picked a {{deck:movement.colour}} or {{deck:group.colour}} card, you have to perform the action it indicates. If you picked a {{deck:reflection.colour}} or {{deck:encounter.colour}} card, take into account what it says, and write a new entry in your journal. If you picked a {{deck:countdown.colour}} card, set it apart. The game ends when the fifth {{deck:countdown.colour}} card is picked. Once you are done with a card, discard it or keep it: it does nothing more in the game, but some players keep their cards as a journal log or as milestones.

ending.p1_html: The game ends when the fifth {{deck:countdown.colour}} card is picked. Each player can add a final entry to their journal, or just leave it as it is. If all players agree, you can end after any number of {{deck:countdown.colour}} cards, or disregard them and use a timer, or stop whenever a story feels complete.
ending.p2: It is okay if your story ends abruptly. You can leave it like that, or return to it on another session.
ending.p3: After ending the game, each player can fill in their character sheet at the back of the player booklet. This way they can see how their character developed during the game: what changed, and what stayed the same.
ending.quote: “The game is not about winning or losing. It is about discovering, exploring, and becoming.”

journal.p1: Unlike traditional games, your character in JOURNEYWAYS emerges through play rather than being predetermined. Use the cards as inspiration, not rigid definitions; the main objective is that you set your imagination free and write the story you want to tell.
journal.p2: Journal entries can be as short or long, as terse or detailed as you want. You can take inspiration from the tile where your token is located and the text on the card, but you can be as creative as you want. Write a journal entry. Doodle it. Draw a comic. Write a fragment. Leave it blank. All of these count.

modes.intro: Two ways to play. Choose either, or move between them.
solo: Remove the {{deck:group.colour}} cards from the game.
Take as much time as you need.

open.returning_body: JOURNEYWAYS is designed for ongoing play. Return to previous sessions, revisit old insights, see how your understanding has evolved. Your character and story continue to develop between sessions.
open.makeyourown_body: Add your own story cards, tiles, character elements, mechanics. Templates are open. JOURNEYWAYS is a framework for exploration; make it your own.
